WHAT TO FIX BY HAND
- B04 and B14: the form wants Day/Month/Year. If your passport prints these dates another way (for example "15 JAN 1990"), rewrite them as DD/MM/YYYY when you copy them onto the form.
- B05: the form splits place of birth into City, Province and Country. Split your place of birth into those three parts by hand, and add "Philippines" as the country if the passport doesn't show it.
- B01 and B02: copy the names exactly as the passport prints them, capitals included. Put the given and middle names in the order the passport uses.
- B11: I ticked Ordinary because a holiday trip is normally made on an ordinary passport. Check your passport and change the tick if it says something else.
- B27: if +65 8555 0143 is a mobile number with no landline, keep it under Mobile No. and write "None" under Tel. If it is a landline, put it only under Tel. and add your mobile number by hand.
- B13: the passport often shows the place of issue next to the issuing authority (B15). If so, copy that city into B13.

STILL NEEDED (NEEDS-YOU)
- B03, B09, B10: other names, other nationalities, and any government ID number
- B13: passport place of issue
- B22: airline and flight
- B23, B24: name, phone number and address of at least your first hotel. Consulates usually expect an itinerary with your accommodation, so book or choose your Tokyo and Kyoto hotels first. If the consulate allows it, you can list every hotel and write "see attached itinerary"
- B28: email address
- B30, B31: your employer's name, phone number and address (the hospital or clinic)
- B36 to B41: tick Yes or No yourself. These are your own sworn answers, so I won't tick them for you
- B43: the date you submit the form
